PyroWave codec, vendored for the Aurora TV client. This tree is a verbatim copy;
do not edit it by hand. To refresh it, rerun vendor-pyrowave.ps1 (from the host
repository) against the pinned commits and copy the result over pyrowave/, or
add a patch under patches/ and re-run the script.

Copied on 2026-09-30 from the host's already-vendored tree at
    /home/jonas/projects/gaming/Vibepollo/third-party/pyrowave/pyrowave
which vendor-pyrowave.ps1 had produced from the upstream commits below.

pyrowave:        186f0393b77f7755953b5ecde994bb1cec2e4155 (https://github.com/Themaister/pyrowave)
Granite:         b6cffd5ce81f540f0855e6778428483e14763d9b (https://github.com/Themaister/Granite)
volk:            47cddf7ed97b94118a08aacb548a411188e016cc
vulkan-headers:  6802bb4733b63ed5efd3adb308a6c885ef180ea1

The PyroWave bitstream carries no version field. The host (Vibepollo) and this
client must be built from the same pyrowave commit; the RTSP handshake advertises
it as PYROWAVE_BITSTREAM_ID = "186f0393". If the two sides ever disagree, the
handshake must reject the codec rather than decode a corrupt stream.

patches/ holds the local changes vendor-pyrowave.ps1 re-applies on top of the
upstream commits; they are copied here for provenance. They do not change the
bitstream format:

  0001-encoder-buffer-pool.patch       Pools the encoder's host/GPU bitstream and
                                       metadata buffers across frames.
  0002-payload-data-444-sizing.patch   Sizes the 4:4:4 payload scratch correctly.
  0003-decoder-reject-short-block.patch Rejects a block record whose payload_words
                                       is smaller than the header, so network input
                                       cannot spin the decoder forever.

The Aurora build wrapper for this tree is CMakeLists.txt next to this file; it is
Aurora's own file, not part of the vendored tree.
